issue.title: Investigate projection-backed bead reads
issue.description: Deferred by epic bead sase-en in plans:202608/bead_show_speed.md; not caused by that epic. The current canonical event store is 8.6 MB while issues.jsonl is 3.0 MB. Fresh-process measurements on the integrated tree average 128.4 ms for sase_core_rs.bead_read_store versus 77.3 ms for bead_read_legacy_jsonl, making the projection read 1.66x faster. Scope: determine a correctness-safe freshness contract for preferring a projection, including mutation atomicity, drift detection, crash recovery, aliases/config validation, and fallback to canonical reduction; implement only if those invariants can be proven and regression-tested.

payload.close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-05: deliberately deprioritized, not fixed. This is an open-ended investigation deferred from epic sase-en, and its own scope makes the payoff conditional — a 1.66x fresh-process read win (128.4ms canonical vs 77.3ms projection) is gated on proving mutation atomicity, drift detection, crash recovery, and a safe fallback for a projection that is explicitly a generated artifact. That correctness bar is high relative to the win, and the cheaper, unconditional startup wins were kept instead (sase-eu, the 12.9x LibYAML config-parse change). Reopen with a +1 if bead read latency becomes a measured user-facing problem.
